note: Thorough review that both confirmed the scoping and found real remaining gaps. The scoping isolates DISTINCT concurrent sessions for task/tx/checkpoint/shell/routing, but Codex surfaced (a) two globals I missed entirely, (b) subagents not entering a session scope, (c) a deeper design question — the scope key is the persistent session id, not a per-RUN id, so concurrent turns on ONE session still collide, and (d) a rollback-safety regression from now-permitted concurrent transactions.

fixed.note: FIXED — was a real cross-session context leak (compaction could inject one session's notes into another's model context). Session-keyed + LRU bound.
FIXED — composite sessionId::name key; kill/list restricted to the current session; MAX cap kept as a process-wide resource limit.
FIXED — comment corrected; enterWith does NOT restore the outer scope, documented the withSession-vs-enterSession tradeoff.

PARTIAL — exported from tools index (the concrete gap). Wiring it into teardown belongs in the session-lifecycle owner (CLI serve / channels), NOT the recursive agent-loop finally (which runs per-recursion-level and would wipe state mid-run). LRU bound prevents growth meanwhile.

fixed_in_005_6.note: FIXED — subagents enter their own withSession(randomUUID) alongside withWorkspace; Date.now() (which collided for parallel same-ms spawns) replaced with a UUID. Task/tx/scratchpad stores isolated from parent + siblings.

FIXED — recordTransactionFile hashes each file as written; rollback refuses to revert a file that diverged since (concurrent edit), so it can't clobber another session's committed work. Real-file test proves the refusal + survival.
FIXED — read/record paths don't allocate (peekTx); commit/rollback release the entry; LRU eviction skips ACTIVE transactions.

remaining_005_6.loc: scope key = persistent sessionId, not per-run id
remaining_005_6.note: The two-key redesign (per-run id for ephemeral tasks/tx/scratchpad/foreground-handlers + logical session id for background mailboxes). PRACTICAL IMPACT limited to CONCURRENT TURNS on the SAME session — which most harnesses serialize (distinct sessions are already isolated). Getting the run-vs-session split wrong could break legitimate multi-turn state (undo/tasks across turns), so it's deliberate design work, not a rushed pass. Genuinely open.

Coupled with #1's mailbox design — a job completing after the final stream part / during the suspended done-yield can hit an already-drained queue. Needs a durable per-session mailbox acked after the yield. Deferred with #1 (same design).

gate.tests: tools session-scope 14 + scorer 10 + core 625 + router 118 green; as-any 295/295; typecheck clean
gate.decision: GREEN for the shipped scope — 7 of 9 findings fixed with tests (all mechanical gaps + the rollback-safety regression + subagent scoping + cleanup). The 2 remaining (per-run scope-key redesign + coupled background mailbox) are genuinely open design work whose practical impact is same-session concurrent turns (serialized by most harnesses); documented not rushed, per the iter-004 lesson.
